failure_patterns.pattern: rule_ignored: The archive line held the clue followed by the answer ('| a bouncer. right: Frank.', '| a eucalyptus tree'). The agent answered the contestant name 'Frank' or shortened the archived answer to 'Eucalyptus'.

rejected_edits.content:
- 'Her/His home / birthplace / house / tomb / museum / statue ... is now a museum / landmark / park' asks for the PERSON the place is about, not the place. Passages are titled with the place ('Susan B. Anthony Museum & House'), but the answer is the name inside it ('Susan B. Anthony'). Strip words like Museum, House, Home, Park, Memorial.
- A clue that is just a bare list of names ('Edward Kennedy, John Kerry', 'Finland, Norway, Sweden') asks for what links the items. Prefer a single entity that all items share, such as a state, country, team, party or role (two senators -> their state, Massachusetts). Do not just repeat one person from the list. Before answering with an umbrella term, check that it contains EVERY item exactly ('Scandinavia' does not strictly include Finland). If no umbrella fits, answer with the listed item that the passages treat as the common or central member.
- A bare 'Title + Person name' or lone proper noun with no verb ('President Tran Duc Luong', 'Timonium') is a category-style clue. Answer with the country, state or larger entity that all the passages tie it to ('Vietnam'), not the title or role ('President of Vietnam').
- A bare quotation, line of verse or lyric with no 'this ...' pointer (e.g. '"I think that I shall never see a poem lovely as a tree"') asks for its CREATOR or speaker (Joyce Kilmer), not the title of the work. Passages that repeat the line next to a name give the answer. Answer with the title only if the clue says 'this poem / this song / this phrase'. If the quote has a gap ('...'), the answer is still the missing word (see above).
rejected_edits.target: The context passages about the topic usually reveal the link.

rejected_edits.content:
- Never attach a noun that the clue already supplies to the answer. Test: substitute your answer for 'this X' / 'these X' in the clue; if the sentence now repeats a word ('the 1945 conference in Yalta Conference', 'gravy made with giblet gravy'), delete the repeated word. 'The 1945 conference in this Crimean city' -> 'Yalta' (not 'Yalta Conference'). 'Gravy made with these turkey innards' -> 'Giblets' (not 'Giblet gravy'). Give the bare head noun or name, in the plural if the clue says 'these'.
- Do not over-qualify the answer with a role, type or modifier phrase built from the passages. 'President of Vietnam' -> 'Vietnam'. 'Amazon River' -> 'Amazon' (drop River/Lake/Mountains when the bare name is standard and the clue does not use the word). 'speech balloon' -> 'balloon' when the clue defines a generic term. Keep a type word only when it is part of the standard proper name or substance name ('World War II', 'Hundred Years' War', 'hydrochloric acid').
- For 'type of this material / traditional color / this one' clues, give the single bare common noun or adjective the passages tie to the clue's anchor, with no modifiers copied from the clue (e.g. 'neoprene is a synthetic type of this material' -> 'rubber', not 'synthetic rubber'; 'the traditional color of London's double-decker buses' -> 'red').
rejected_edits.target: do not append that role word to the answer.

rejected_edits.content:
- CHECK the category noun and every descriptor before answering. If the clue says 'caustic ACID', the answer must be an acid (hydrochloric acid), not a base from a nearby passage (sodium hydroxide). If the clue says 'rare mammal found in Florida', the answer must live in Florida (manatee), even if a passage says 'a relative of the dugong'. A relative, component or variable in the passages is only an anchor.
- 'Its area/volume/circumference equals <formula>' or 'its <property> is ...' asks for the WHOLE object that has that property (Circle), not a variable in the formula (radius).
- 'One of these <X>' / 'this <noun>' with a generic noun: the answer is the common noun or category the description defines, never a word already in the clue ('water-filled one of these holes' -> 'sinkhole', not 'spring'; 'the guy hired to throw unruly people out of bars' -> 'bouncer'). 'This war / this city / this river' needs an entity of exactly that type. A person from an unrelated passage that merely shares words with the clue ('Themistocles') is wrong.
- 'This <state/city/country>' clues often give only a landmark, event, institution or border as the anchor ('lighting of Temple Square', 'university in Chapel Hill', 'boundary with Ciudad Juarez'). Answer the place the passages repeatedly tie to that anchor, as a bare name ('Salt Lake City', 'North Carolina', 'El Paso'). Drop the landmark, the institution word ('University of ...') and any state or country suffix.
rejected_edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?

rejected_edits.content:
- If no passage mentions the clue's key event or fact (a particular 'sabbatical', scandal, record, quote or superlative), do NOT default to the best-documented entity that fits only the generic descriptors (e.g. the longest-serving or most recent mayor). Use your own trivia knowledge of who or what that distinctive fact belongs to ('material cost greater than all other wars put together' -> 'World War II'). Prefer a candidate that appears in the passages and whose time period and role fit; consider the person famous for the headline-making event (a scandal-linked mayor) over one who merely held the office.
- Likewise, when the passages are noisy or off-topic but the descriptors point to a famous, unambiguous item ('giant flour tortilla wrapped around meat, beans & cheese' at Chipotle -> 'burrito'), answer from general knowledge. Never refuse.
rejected_edits.target: - Otherwise, build the answer from passages that match several of the clue's details.
